exams: NEB +2 Science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (50 percent) for medicine
English test only if the university asks
abroad_add.work: Not checked yet. Treat part time work as unavailable and budget your whole stay.
abroad_add.note: Mostly a medicine destination. State medical institutes in Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara, Andijan and Fergana teach in English; quoted tuition is USD 2,500 to 4,000 a year on one list and up to USD 7,500 on another, living about USD 500 to 650 a month, and the course is six years with the internship. One university asks for a bank statement of USD 5,000 to 6,000. Many agency pages say NMC approved, which usually means the National Medical Commission of India. For Nepal what counts is Nepal Medical Council recognition of the college and course before you pay, then the NMCLE after you return. Ask for a written fee letter. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175 and USD 1 about NPR 145.

exams: IELTS or TOEFL for English taught programmes
CAPLE Portuguese test for Portuguese taught programmes
abroad_add.intakes: September; applications usually March to July
abroad_add.work: Not checked on an official page. Agency guides say up to 20 hours a week in term and full time in holidays; one guide says there is no weekly cap. Confirm with AIMA and your university.
abroad_add.note: Public universities charge non EU students EUR 1,500 to 7,000 a year (most EUR 3,500 to 7,000; medicine EUR 16,500 to 18,000 at Lisbon and Porto in 2026/27). Bachelor degrees are mostly in Portuguese (B1 at Lisbon, B2 at Coimbra); English is realistic at master level and at economics and management schools such as Nova SBE, ISEG and Catolica. Funds are pegged to the minimum wage: about EUR 760 a month, EUR 9,120 for a year, and the figure changes every year. Apply for the D4 study visa, then the residence permit through AIMA. Living is EUR 700 to 1,100 a month. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175 and USD 1 about NPR 145.

exams: University admission test for some programmes
abroad_add.work: Sources disagree. The European Commission country page says non EU students can work up to 40 hours a week once they hold the temporary residence permit; several agencies say 20 hours in term and full time in holidays. Ask the Migration Department and your university before you plan around work.
abroad_add.note: More than 500 English taught programmes. The European Commission lists bachelor tuition from EUR 1,300 and master from EUR 2,300 a year; agencies quote EUR 3,950 to 8,500 for non EU students and EUR 12,800 to 14,100 for medicine at Vilnius and Kaunas (LSMU). Living EUR 500 to 800 a month. Proof of funds is quoted from EUR 500 to about EUR 1,200 a month depending on the source, health insurance is compulsory, and one guide says Nepali applicants use the Lithuanian Embassy in New Delhi. Check the current figures with the Migration Department. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175 and USD 1 about NPR 145.
abroad_add.stay_back: 12 months to look for work after graduating

exams: IELTS 6.5 at most universities (HKU asks 6.0 in writing and speaking)
abroad_add.intakes: September; applications open from September of the year before
abroad_add.work: The default rule for full time degree students is on campus work up to 20 hours a week, summer work from 1 June to 31 August with no limit, and study related internships. Since November 2024 degree students on local programmes have been temporarily exempt from the hour limits, but the Immigration Department still calls the exemption temporary. Permission arrives as a No Objection Letter with your visa.
abroad_add.note: Non local bachelor tuition for 2027/28 is about USD 27,000 to 36,000 a year; research postgraduate places at the eight public universities cost about USD 6,400. No tuition free route, so scholarships matter (HKPFS for PhD). The university sponsors your student visa (government fee HKD 330, about six weeks). Living including a hall place is about USD 8,700 to 14,300 a year. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175 and USD 1 about NPR 145.
abroad_add.stay_back: 24 months under IANG with no job offer if you apply within 6 months of graduating

cz.work: A long term study permit carries the right to work without a separate work permit and the employer must report the job to the labour office. Agencies say a 20 hour weekly cap applies; a 2026 guide says there is no weekly cap. Read the Ministry of the Interior (MV CR) rules for your permit.

ge.work: Not clear in law. Two agency guides say a student with a residence permit can work up to 20 hours a week; another says no law covers student work so part time jobs are informal. Do not count on income; ask the Public Service Hall and your university.

bd.work: Not allowed. The S student visa carries the endorsement employment in Bangladesh prohibited (Visa Policy 2026) and a breach can lead to cancellation. There is no student work allowance and no post study work period.

kg.work: Agencies disagree. Some say part time work is allowed after you convert to a multiple entry status with a valid permit and the approval of the migration service; others say a student visa does not encourage jobs for medical students. Plan to pay for your studies without wages.

kz.work: Agencies say students may work part time, usually up to 20 hours a week in term and full time in holidays, only with the university authorisation and within limits set by the labour ministry. No official page was read, so confirm with your university before you accept a job.

ph.work: A 9(f) student visa does not allow work. Limited short jobs or internships need a Special Work Permit from the Bureau of Immigration (agencies quote 3 to 6 months) with a school endorsement; working without one risks fines, visa cancellation or deportation.

scholarships_add.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
scholarships_add.covers: Annual stipend of HKD 344,400 (HKD 28,700 a month) and HKD 14,400 a year for conference and research travel, for up to three years; 400 fellowships for 2027/28
scholarships_add.who: Open to every nationality. New full time PhD students at the eight participating Hong Kong universities, judged on academic record, research ability, communication and leadership. You must also meet the admission rules of your university and programme and show English proof (IELTS or a degree taught in English).
scholarships_add.how: Register on the HKPFS electronic system for a reference number before you apply to a university. The 2027/28 deadline is 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong time, so for a later start the next call opens in the autumn of 2027.

scholarships_add.name: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship (University of Toronto)
scholarships_add.covers: Tuition, books, incidental fees and residence for four years
scholarships_add.who: Outstanding international students about to start their first university degree at Toronto. Your school must take part in the programme and nominate you (one student per school each year). You also apply for admission to at least one undergraduate programme.
scholarships_add.how: For September 2027 entry the school nomination closed on 9 October 2026, the admission application on 16 October 2026 and the scholarship form on 6 November 2026, so all three are shut. Expect the same months in 2027; ask your counsellor to register the school in July.

s-mgss.how: The 2026-27 window on goischolarship.com.np ran from 23 October to 15 November 2026 (the portal closed at 00.00 on 16 November). Apply directly; the Embassy does not accept applications through consultants or agents. Awardees send the Class 11 mark sheet and a promotion certificate by 31 December to continue in Class 12.

s-gjss.how: The 2026-27 window on goischolarship.com.np ran from 23 October to 15 November 2026. You must be a regular first year bachelor student (not diploma) aged 17 to 22 on 1 July 2027 with a Class 12 mark sheet, and not receiving any other scholarship. Continuation each year needs the mark sheet and a promotion certificate by 31 December. Apply directly, not through agents.

s-homi-bhabha.how: The 2026-27 notice closed on 4 June 2026: age 25 or less on 1 July 2026, at least 60 percent aggregate in BE and at least 50 percent in English in Class 12, an application fee of NPR 400 paid at Nepal SBI Bank, and the form sent by post or handed in at the Embassy. Only completed bachelor degrees count.

s-sh.how: Apply on the Tempus Public Foundation portal (apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu). The 2026-27 call came out on 28 October 2025 and closed on 15 January 2026 at 2 pm Central European Time. For 2027-28 expect the same pattern (portal in mid November, deadline about 15 January 2027) but the call was not published when this was checked in early November 2026. Nepali applicants also complete the national partner step, then sit the university exam or interview from March to May.

s-pu-scholarship.how: Pokhara University runs several calls a year. The master scholarship entrance for Fall 2026 took applications from 26 August to 21 September 2026 (60 percent open, 40 percent reserved for disabled, martyr and conflict families, remote, Dalit, Janajati and Madhesi students, half of each for women, bachelor completed within three years). A call for vacant undergraduate scholarship seats was published on 4 November 2026; read the notice for its deadline. One summary lists 1,328 bachelor scholarship seats for 2083 (Science and Technology 501, Management 788, Humanities 39).

For a foreign +2 or A level, first get the HSEB equivalence at Sanothimi (about NPR 500 for HSEB board papers, NPR 1,000 for A level)

Fill the equivalence form and pay NPR 1,000 at Nepal Bank when the university is already recognised by TU, or NPR 4,000 when it is not

If the university is not recognised, add the syllabus, thesis or project report and a translation when the paper is not in English
in person
Collect the certificate when the Centre calls you; an online registration route exists on tucdc.edu.np

Syllabus and thesis for a non recognised university

guides_add.name: Study MBBS abroad and practise in Nepal
steps: Before you pay anything, confirm that the college and the course are recognised by the Nepal Medical Council and listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools
online
Check the minimum: NEB +2 Science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, around 50 percent or GPA 2.4, and age 17 in the year of admission
online
Get the NOC from the Ministry of Education, then the attested documents, before the visa
in person
Finish the course and the internship the college requires
in person
Return and pass the Nepal Medical Council licensing exam (NMCLE) to register; it is computer based
in person
docs: NOC from the Ministry of Education
Written fee letter from the college

faq_add.q: Is a foreign MBBS valid in Nepal?
faq_add.a: Only if the Nepal Medical Council recognises the college and the course, and you then pass the NMCLE licensing exam and register after your internship. Check recognition before you pay a deposit, and keep the college fee letter and the recognition proof together.

faq_add.q: An agency says its MBBS college is NMC approved. Does that count for Nepal?
faq_add.a: Not necessarily. Most agency pages mean the National Medical Commission of India, which is a different body. For a Nepali graduate the Nepal Medical Council recognition is the one that matters. Ask the Council, not the agency, and read the college entry on the World Directory of Medical Schools.

faq_add.q: What does MBBS in Uzbekistan cost?
faq_add.a: Two agency lists quote tuition of USD 2,500 to 4,000 a year and up to USD 7,500, with living near USD 500 to 650 a month, over six years including the internship. That is roughly NPR 3.6 to 10.9 lakh a year for tuition alone at USD 1 about NPR 145. The work rule is not checked, so assume no income. Ask for a written fee letter and confirm Nepal Medical Council recognition first.

faq_add.q: Can I work while studying in Bangladesh, the Philippines, Georgia or Czechia?
faq_add.a: Bangladesh: no, the student visa prohibits employment. Philippines: not on the student visa alone, a Special Work Permit is needed. Georgia: unclear, guides say 20 hours but others say jobs are informal. Czechia: yes without a separate work permit, but sources disagree on a 20 hour cap. Always confirm with the immigration office and your university.

faq_add.q: Can I really work 40 hours a week as a student in Lithuania?
faq_add.a: The European Commission country page says non EU students can work up to 40 hours a week once they hold the temporary residence permit. Several agencies say 20 hours in term. Because sources disagree, ask the Lithuanian Migration Department and your university before you plan your budget around wages.

faq_add.q: How much does it cost to study in Portugal?
faq_add.a: Public universities charge non EU students EUR 1,500 to 7,000 a year, with most programmes at EUR 3,500 to 7,000 and medicine at EUR 16,500 to 18,000 in 2026/27. Living is EUR 700 to 1,100 a month. For the visa, show about EUR 760 a month (EUR 9,120 a year); the figure follows the minimum wage and changes. Bachelor degrees are mostly in Portuguese.

faq_add.q: Can I work while studying in Hong Kong and stay after?
faq_add.a: Full time degree students may work on campus up to 20 hours a week and take summer jobs and internships; since November 2024 a temporary exemption has lifted the hour limits for local degree programmes, and your No Objection Letter shows what applies. After graduating you can apply within six months for 24 months under IANG without a job offer.

faq_add.q: Is there a fully funded PhD in Hong Kong open to Nepalis?
faq_add.a: Yes, the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme. It pays HKD 344,400 a year plus HKD 14,400 for travel for up to three years and is open to every nationality. For 2027/28 you register for a reference number by 1 December 2026 at noon Hong Kong time, and you still need admission from a participating university.

faq_add.q: How do I get my certificates attested for a visa or a university abroad?
faq_add.a: Nepal does not use the apostille. Get the paper verified by the issuing board or university, apply to the Department of Consular Services (Tripureshwor) through the Nepal E-Attestation System or its appointment portal, pay the fee (law firm guides quote NPR 500 a document), collect the stamp and, if the country asks, legalise it at its embassy in Kathmandu. See the guide for the steps.

faq_add.q: What is a TU equivalence certificate and who needs one?
faq_add.a: It states that a foreign or non TU qualification matches a TU one. You need it when a Nepali university, office or employer asks for that proof. The Curriculum Development Centre charges NPR 1,000 when the university is already recognised by TU and NPR 4,000 when it is not; a foreign +2 first needs HSEB equivalence. Check the fee at the window before you pay.

faq_add.q: When did the Indian Embassy scholarship (MGSS and GJSS) close this year?
faq_add.a: The 2026-27 window on goischolarship.com.np ran from 23 October to 15 November 2026 for MGSS (Class 11) and GJSS (first year bachelor). Both need an application made directly, not through an agent, and awardees send mark sheets by 31 December each year. The next call is expected in the same autumn months.

faq_add.q: How do Pokhara University scholarship seats work?
faq_add.a: The university runs central scholarship entrance rounds and publishes calls for vacant seats during the year, the latest on 4 November 2026. Seats are split between open merit and reserved groups (disabled, martyr and conflict families, remote, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi), with half of each for women. Read the notice for the deadline.

faq_add.q: Can I get a scholarship for a bachelor degree abroad?
faq_add.a: A few exist. The Lester B. Pearson scholarship at the University of Toronto needs school nomination and ran to 6 November 2026 for September 2027 entry. Turkiye Burslari, Stipendium Hungaricum and some university awards also take bachelor students. Start the application a full year ahead.

faq_add.q: When does the Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28 call open?
faq_add.a: The last call was published on 28 October 2025 and closed on 15 January 2026. For 2027/28 the call was not out in early November 2026, but expect the portal in mid November and a deadline about 15 January 2027. Watch stipendiumhungaricum.hu and prepare marks, a motivation letter and the national partner step.

faq_add.q: What is open now at Nepal Rastra Bank?
faq_add.a: A call of 2083 Kartik 27 lists 61 posts: 26 Assistant Director (Administration), 3 Accounts and Audit (CA, ACCA or CPA), 2 Commercial Law, 4 Information Technology and 26 Assistant (+2 with a valid PSC preliminary certificate). Apply online by 2083 Mangsir 17 (about 2 December 2026); a double fee window runs to Mangsir 24 (about 9 December). Read the notice for age and group fees.

faq_add.q: What does the BBA and MBA at Kathmandu University School of Management cost?
faq_add.a: The school lists the whole BBA (Emphasis) at NPR 9,60,000 plus a NPR 10,000 refundable deposit, with Honours courses costing extra, and the whole MBA package at NPR 6,56,000 in 12 instalments. The application fee is NPR 1,500 and a tuition waiver is possible for needy students after admission. Confirm on the school site because the figures can change.

faq_add.q: How much money must I show for a South Korea student visa?
faq_add.a: Guides disagree. One says KRW 9,000,000 (about USD 6,800) from three months of statements; others say about USD 20,000 including tuition, with the sponsor six month statements. The university and the Korean Embassy in Kathmandu set the rule, so get the figure from them in writing and also prepare the MoEST NOC.

faq_add.q: Do I need a Japanese language test before I apply to a school in Japan?
faq_add.a: For a language school, yes: JLPT N5 or an equal test (NAT-TEST 5Q or J-CERT) or about 150 hours of study is the usual proof. Degree programmes taught in Japanese ask for N2 or higher. Your school applies for the Certificate of Eligibility, which takes about 2 to 3 months, before you apply at the Embassy of Japan in Kathmandu.

note_add.p-ku-school: Official fees (school website, Fall 2026 intake): the whole BBA (Emphasis) programme is NPR 9,60,000 plus a refundable caution deposit of NPR 10,000, and Honours students pay extra for the Honours courses; the whole MBA package is NPR 6,56,000 (deposit included), payable in 12 instalments, books and accommodation extra. The application fee is NPR 1,500. SAARC students pay 1.5 times and other international students 2 times the MBA fee. BBA entry needs +2 with at least 40 percent or CGPA 1.6 and a D+ in each subject, then the entrance test, statement of objectives and interview; needy and deserving students can apply for a tuition waiver after admission. Figures can change without notice.

govt_note_add.g-so: A Public Service Commission notice reported on 14 November 2026 invites applications for gazetted third class posts (Section Officer or equal) in the civil, federal parliament and national human rights services and for Health Service 7th and 8th level posts; promotion applicants must submit by 2083 Mangsir 25 and the technical written exams start on 2083 Chaitra 14. Read the notice on psc.gov.np for the open competition groups, fee and dates.
govt_note_add.g-nrb: Current call (notice of 2083 Kartik 27): 61 vacancies, all online at jobs.nrb.org.np. Assistant Director (Administration) 26 seats, Accounts and Audit 3, Commercial Law 2, Information Technology 4, and Assistant (Second Class) 26. Applications close on 2083 Mangsir 17 (about 2 December 2026) and the double fee window ends on Mangsir 24 (about 9 December); age and certificates are counted on Mangsir 17. Fees are NPR 1,000 for one group and NPR 400 for each more for Assistant Director, NPR 800 and NPR 300 for Assistant. Assistant applicants must hold a valid Public Service Commission preliminary qualification certificate (Kharidar, Level 4 or Level 5 equivalent) issued within one year. Age at the deadline: Assistant Director 21 to 35 years for men and up to 40 for women; Assistant 18 to 35 and up to 40 for women. The IT group adds a practical test run by the bank. Probation is 1 year for men and 6 months for women, with a contribution based pension.

abroad_note_add.kr: Proof of funds for the D-2 degree visa is quoted differently: one 2026 guide says a statement of at least KRW 9,000,000 (about USD 6,800) from three months of bank statements; two Nepali consultancies say about USD 20,000 including tuition, with sponsor statements. Universities and the Embassy of Korea in Kathmandu set the rule, so ask them. The visa fee is quoted at KRW 60,000 and the MoEST NOC is part of the file.
abroad_note_add.jp: Language schools ask for JLPT N5 or an equal test (NAT-TEST 5Q, J-CERT) or about 150 hours of study; most degree programmes in Japanese want N2. The school applies for the Certificate of Eligibility (about 2 to 3 months), then you apply at the Embassy of Japan in Kathmandu (2 to 4 weeks, visa fee quoted at NPR 3,000 to 5,000). Sponsor fund figures vary from JPY 1.5 million to 3 million between guides, so use the figure your school gives in writing.
